market_holds: Spot 7.825 at the 18:09 UTC seal (sealed baseline). The straddle to 20 Nov implies 10.86%, but the ATM spread is 40% of mid and 20d realised vol is 103% because the window includes the election crash, so the event part cannot be read cleanly off the chain. Since the 26 Oct crash (11.48 to 8.33, -27%, after Lula's runoff win) STNE has moved in step with PAGS (8.56 to 7.86) and below EWZ. Its own 5d run-up of +4.5% matches PAGS and EWZ, so the run-in is the Brazil tape, not company news (Yahoo daily bars, my own arithmetic). Consensus: Q3 EPS $0.49 and revenue $715m (Earnings Whispers preview, 4 Nov). Local previews are bearish. Itaú BBA has adjusted net income at R$571m (-11% y/y), gross profit at R$1.6bn and cost of risk near 21%. Safra has R$553m (-13.8% y/y) with card volume down. Itaú cut its 2026 profit estimate 10% (Finsiders, Nov). FY26 guidance is adjusted gross profit R$6.6-7.0bn and adjusted EPS R$10.8-11.4. H1 delivered R$3.05bn of gross profit and R$4.58 of EPS, and management said in August it was aiming for the low end. The 2027 guide is R$7.2-8.3bn gross profit and R$11.8-13.4 EPS, set when Selic was assumed at 12.5%. Selic is about 14%, and UBS says the curve steepened about 250bp after the runoff. Sell-side cut targets after the election: UBS to Neutral, $15 to $8.50 (5 Nov); Goldman Hold at $9.50 (30 Oct). Short interest rose from 9.2m to 15.2m shares between the 15 Oct and 30 Oct settlements, 1.9 days to cover (Nasdaq). On the stated 2027 guide the stock is roughly 3.5x earnings, against 15x as its five-year average.
view: Two things are close to certain in this print, and both are already in the price and the previews. First, the FY26 gross-profit floor needs about R$1.77bn a quarter in H2. Q2 was R$1.56bn and Itaú expects about R$1.6bn for Q3, so a cut to around R$6.3-6.4bn, or a 'below the range' message, is arithmetic, and the Earnings Whispers preview spells it out. Second, the 2027 guide was built on a 12.5% Selic, and after the runoff the curve is about 250bp higher on a business whose net financial expenses run at 30% of revenue. That guide is likely to be cut or withdrawn. That is the line STNE trades on: the March 2026 2027 cut produced a -13.8% gap. This time, though, the stock already trades at a 2027 multiple of roughly 3.5x, and the sell-side re-marked its targets after the election. Things that could surprise upward: credit stabilising (Itaú BBA saw first-payment defaults peaking in February, and government-backed lines are lowering cost of risk), and a larger or accelerated buyback at a price that makes each real very accretive. Tier 1 is 26% and R$3bn was returned in the twelve months to June. Things that could surprise downward: NPL>90 still rising (it went 6.98% to 8.60% in Q2), another one-off like Q2's R$200m issuer provision, and a 2027 guide withdrawn without a number. Nu and Inter report the same evening and share the Brazil-fintech factor, so a large part of the morning-after move will be sector tape, not STNE. I cannot show one side of the deciding line is more likely than this price assumes, so no recommendation. I keep a slight negative lean from the company's record of negative reactions to guide revisions.

recommendation.reason: A guide cut is the likely headline, but it is visible in previews (the H2 arithmetic) and in post-election target cuts, and the stock is at roughly 3.5x the stated 2027 guide. Since the runoff it has tracked PAGS and EWZ almost exactly, so no company-specific gap is showing. Credit and capital return could break either way, and there is no dated evidence on which way. Nu and Inter report the same night and add correlated noise.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A large new buyback for the next year with credit metrics stabilising (NPL>90 flat or down, coverage up) would make a long likely right. A withdrawn 2027 guide plus another one-off provision would make a short likely right.

self_critique: At about 3.5x earnings with 26% Tier 1 and a record of large buybacks, any sign that credit is stabilising, plus a capital-return announcement, could produce a sharp relief gap even if the guide is cut, as the AGBK +15% today may hint for Brazilian fintech prints. Equally, the March 2026 precedent (-13.8% on a 2027 cut) shows the market punishes Stone guide cuts even when they are expected. I may be underweighting both tails, but neither favours one side on evidence I can date.
approach_notes: P6 (take the run-in apart against peers) was decisive: STNE vs PAGS since the election showed the whole move was the tape. P4 helped in showing the guide-cut arithmetic is already in previews. The playbook offers little for a name whose reaction is dominated by same-night peer prints and macro.
